title: Rendering HTML with EJS
idea: A template is an HTML file with holes in it. EJS fills the holes with your data, and `res.render` sends the finished HTML.
points: Run `npm install ejs`, then `app.set('view engine', 'ejs')` once; Express loads it by name.
`res.render('books', { books })` fills `views/books.ejs`; the object's keys become variables.
`<%= x %>` escapes HTML in the value; `<%- x %>` prints it raw.
`<% %>` runs JavaScript, such as a loop, and prints nothing.

walk.text: Plain HTML is copied to the output unchanged.
`<% %>` runs JavaScript and prints nothing. `-%>` also removes the newline after the tag.
`<%= %>` prints a value with its HTML characters escaped.

code.title: Render a page
code.caption: A route renders the template with data from the model. Press Run for the real output.

walk.text: Import Express and the same model the JSON API uses.
Add a book whose title contains markup, as a user might submit.
`app.set('view engine', 'ejs')` makes Express load `ejs` and look for `.ejs` files.
`res.render('books', data)` finds `views/books.ejs`, fills it, and sends the HTML.
Request the page and print the status and the content type.
Print the HTML. The markup in the title is escaped, so a browser shows it as text.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Never print user text with `<%-`: it skips escaping and allows script injection.
Pass every variable the template uses; a missing one throws `ReferenceError` at render time.
Start Node from the project root: Express looks for `views/` in the current folder.

quiz.why: `<%=` escapes the value, so `&` becomes `&`. `<%-` prints it exactly as given.

takeaway: Treat a template as a function: same data in, same HTML out.
